extracted.intended_audience: Applicants (inventors, companies) and representatives preparing and filing German utility model (Gebrauchsmuster) applications with the DPMA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for drafting and filing utility model applications (Gebrauchsmuster) at the German Patent and Trade Mark Office (DPMA), including what is protectable, required documents, fees, claim/description/drawing drafting rules, and post-filing procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions eligible for utility model protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions (except processes) with new technical features may be eligible for utility model protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility model protection is granted for technical inventions which are new, involve an inventive step and are susceptible of industrial application (section 1 (1) of the Utility Model Act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-registrable inventions (absolute exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following in particular cannot be protected as utility models: discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; aesthetic creations; schemes, rules and methods for performing mental acts (e.g. building plans, dress patterns, teaching methods), for playing games, or for doing business (e.g. rules, accounting systems) and programs for computers; presentations of information (e.g. tables, forms, typographical arrangements); constructions contrary to the laws of nature (e.g. perpetuum mobile); inventions relating to processes (e.g. to manufacture or use); inventions the exploitation of which would be contrary to ordre public or morality; biotechnological inventions (section 1 (2) of the Patent Act); plant and animal varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DPMA examines before registration whether a technical invention having unity has been submitted and whether there isn’t any reason for exclusion regarding non-registrable inventions as listed here. These are absolute requirements for protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention is considered to be new if it does not form part of the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State of the art comprises any knowledge made available to the public by written description or by use in Germany before the relevant date (filing or priority date). A six-month period of grace applies where disclosure is based on the applicant's or predecessor's conception (section 3 (1)). Applicants are recommended to check the state of the art beforehand; DPMA search service may be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject matter of a utility model involves an inventive step if, having regard to the state of the art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive step is a relative requirement which DPMA does not examine prior to registration unless a search is requested; lack of inventive step may be asserted in cancellation or infringement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention is considered susceptible of industrial application if its subject matter can be made or used in any kind of industry, including agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial applicability is a relative requirement; DPMA normally does not examine it prior to registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: For each invention, a separate application must be filed (section 4 (1) sentence 2 of the Utility Model Act); in the case of lack of unity, several applications are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DPMA checks unity prior to registration. The principle of unity also limits how many independent claims can be filed in one application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examination prior to registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to registration, the utility model section examines only if a technical invention having unity has been submitted and whether there isn’t any reason for exclusion regarding non-registrable inventions (absolute requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative requirements (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability) are examined only in cancellation or infringement proceedings or if a DPMA search is requested. Consequently a utility model may be registered even if relative requirements are not met, producing a fictitious title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may call on assistance from advisors experienced in industrial property (lawyer or patent attorney) who may represent the applicant in the registration procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with no residence or principal place of business in Germany must appoint a patent attorney or lawyer entitled to represent them before DPMA and in related proceedings (section 28 (1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A written authorisation must be submitted to the DPMA only if the representative is not a patent attorney, a lawyer or in certain cases a Patentassessor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The representative must have capacity to sue and be sued and the power of attorney must be executed in favour of a person using their civil name. For legal persons the signatory must prove entitlement to sign; DPMA may demand notarisation in case of doubt. General powers of attorney may be registered with DPMA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to file
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be filed at DPMA (Munich), Jena Sub-Office, Information and Service Centre Berlin, and certain patent information centres which note the date of receipt and transmit applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing is possible (see electronic filing criterion). Patent information centres do not examine applications; they forward them and note date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing (DPMAdirektPro) and reduced fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model applications may be filed electronically with the DPMA using DPMAdirektPro; a reduced filing fee is charged for electronic applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal and technical requirements are prescribed in section 21 (1) Utility Model Act in conjunction with section125a of Patent Act and the Ordinance on Electronic Legal Transactions. Technical details available on DPMA website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be filed in a language other than German, but a German translation must be submitted within three months after filing (section 4b). If the translation is not filed in due time, the application will be deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: German translations must be certified by a lawyer or patent attorney or done by an officially authorised translator (section 9 (1) of the Utility Model Ordinance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory documents — Request for registration (form G 6003)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be filed on the form issued by the DPMA (form G 6003) and include required data (mailing address/date, reference/telephone, function of addressee, applicant/representative, numbers, designation of the invention, other requests, explanatory notes, priority, fees, enclosures, signature, function of signatory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and accurate completion of boxes (1)-(13) is necessary; the invention must be described in words to be accorded a filing date; claims, description and drawings (if any) must be furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of the invention (title)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short and technically precise designation of the invention shall be given which corresponds to the title of the description; trademarks or fancy designations are not admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common terms rather than generic placeholders (avoid 'appliance', 'means', 'device'). Innovations should not be anticipated in the designation; innovations belong in the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement of registration/publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request the registration and publication of the invention may be postponed for up to 15 months from filing or priority date (section 8 (1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postponement useful if applicant intends to file in non-Paris-Convention states, prepare commercial exploitation, or await a search result. No industrial property right arises prior to registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search request (DPMA search)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may request ascertainment of the state of the art (search request) either at filing or later; the request is subject to a fee and must be paid within three months after filing the request or is deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search fee is forfeited upon payment and is not refundable even if search is terminated. Consider carefully whether to request a search at filing or later when obstacles to registration are clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division / Splitting off
rubrics_metrics.description: Indications necessary if application results from a division under section 4 (6) or separation from a pending original application; splitting off from earlier patent application is possible by declaration when filing the utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For splitting off the file number and date of the earlier patent application and a copy (and German translation if foreign-language) must be filed; right to splitting off exercisable within specified time limits (see section 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming licences (declaration of interest in licensing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration of being interested in licensing is non-committal; it does not oblige applicant to grant licences but will be entered in the Utility Model Register and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration may be revoked at any time vis-à-vis DPMA and third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority (domestic, foreign, exhibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is generally determined by date of receipt at DPMA. Applicants may claim domestic, foreign (Paris Convention/TRIPS), or exhibition priority within prescribed time limits and must supply required information and copies of earlier applications within deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic priority: within 12 months of earlier filing; claim must be made within two months of later filing for certain particulars; priority documents may need to be filed within 16 months for foreign priority. Exhibition priority: claim within six months from first display; evidence required before 16th month after first display. Failure to timely submit documents forfeits priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees — filing, search, electronic and maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified fees payable: e.g., filing fee (40 euros), electronic filing fee (30 euros), search fee (250 euros) [fee numbers provided], and maintenance fees at years 4-6 (210 euros), 7-8 (350 euros), 9-10 (530 euros).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application or search request deemed withdrawn if filing/search fee not paid within three months of filing. Maintenance fees due after expiry of 3, 6 and 8 years; payment windows, surcharges for late payment, and consequences (lapse) are described. Provide correct file and fee numbers to avoid processing delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment methods and date of payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments may be made by cash at DPMA, transfer to Bundeskasse account, cash deposit at a bank to Bundeskasse account, or submitting a valid SEPA Core Direct Debit Mandate with specification form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date of payment is defined depending on method (cash day of payment; transfer when credited to Bundeskasse; SEPA mandate day of receipt at DPMA). Original SEPA mandate must be submitted; filing fee should be paid after communication of official file number except for SEPA direct debit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure requirement (description and carrying out invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be disclosed in the application in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out without difficulty by a person skilled in the art; claims, a technical description, and drawings if any, must be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a basic requirement at the date of filing; failure to satisfy it cannot be cured later and will prevent registration (application rejected unless a new application is filed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — scope and drafting principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of protection is determined by the terms of the claims (section 12a); claims may be in one part or two parts (preamble and characterising part) and may be arranged feature-wise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two-part claims used, state-of-the-art features go in the preamble using the technical designation from box (6); characterising part introduced by 'characterised in that' or equivalent. Essential features must be in the first (principal) claim; several independent claims allowed if unity respected. Dependent claims must refer to preceding claims and grouped suitably. Claims should not, except where absolutely necessary, rely on references to the description or drawings. Use reference signs to facilitate understanding when drawings present. Number claims consecutively in Arabic numerals. Claims may not contain descriptions of functions, applications and advantages — these belong in the description. Each claim must be introduced by the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description — recommended structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Title must match the designation; recommended to start with the technical field, state of the art and deficiencies, present the technical problem and the means solving it, and explain at least one embodiment with details of particular embodiments; conclude with advantages achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings are referred to, use reference signs; cite documents in full (patents with country and file number; books with author, title, edition, publisher, place, year and page; journals with title, volume/year, number and page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — when required and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are not mandatory but must be filed if the claims or description contain references to them. Photographs are not equivalent to drawings and cannot replace drawings if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings are submitted later and the application contained a reference to them, the date drawings are received by DPMA will be deemed the filing date of the entire application (which may be advantageous). Drawings shall clearly show interaction of features, emphasise essential points, neglect unimportant details, use Arabic numerals as reference signs, have minimum margins per section 7, be in black with clean clear contours, and must not contain explanations (use reference signs instead). Claims, description and drawings must be on separate sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of defects after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If application documents do not comply with certain requirements, consequences differ depending on the defect kind: some basic requirements must be fulfilled at filing date and cannot be complied with later; other requirements may be complied with subsequently upon DPMA notification within a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic defects (e.g., insufficient disclosure) prevent registration and require filing a new application; other defects lead to DPMA requesting compliance and possible rejection if not remedied in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility model section may hear the applicant ex officio or upon written request; a hearing can only take place after prior arrangement and serves to clarify matters aiming at registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing may be used to resolve issues to allow registration; applicant or representative may request hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After payment of required fees, applications without formal deficiencies are recorded in the Utility Model Register and the registration is published in the Patent Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From publication date, IP files are freely accessible electronically via DPMAregister for online inspection; no fee charged for this service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal aid and assignment of representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who cannot pay fees due to personal and economic conditions may be granted legal aid in the registration procedure upon request if there are sufficient prospects of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form A 9541 must be completed. Applicants granted legal aid may be assigned a patent attorney or lawyer of their choice who agrees to represent them, or DPMA may appoint a representative if needed and prior attempts to secure one failed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal presentation rules for drawings and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should respect minimum margins per section 7; presentations in colour are not permitted; drawings should be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals and must not contain explanations; reference signs shall be used for features and may be placed in brackets in the description or in a list of reference signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference signs should be Arabic numerals (or letters where appropriate). Do not include explanatory text in drawings; use a separate list of reference signs if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example-based guidance for novice applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The leaflet provides an example application (description, list of reference signs, claims and drawings) showing structure: state of the art, problem, solution, advantages, figures and explanatory reference signs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting aids: answer questions such as which parts does the device comprise? Where are particular parts located? In what manner are parts connected? Use the example as a model for assembling description and claims; remember scope of protection determined by claims.
